answer: Each agent must lock a bond for 30 days before its identity can bid for work, whether it sells umber pigment or builds a cipher. The bond stays locked even if the agent abandons the account, so creating 1,000 eligible identities requires 1,000 bonds tied up for the full period. This makes the fable of free, unlimited identities economically false: an attacker must finance every fake bidder, paying the opportunity cost of immobilized capital.
